questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface
questions.problem:
Find the surface area of the parametric surface defined by the equations 

$$
x=u,\,y={v}^{2},\,z=\frac{2}{3}{v}^{3}
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le \sqrt{3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,{v}^{2},\,\frac{2}{3}{v}^{3}⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(\frac{2}{3}{v}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(\frac{2}{3}{v}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,2{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2v & 2{v}^{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 2v & 2{v}^{2}\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2{v}^{2}\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2{v}^{2},\,2v⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨0,\,-2{v}^{2},\,2v⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2{v}^{2})^{2}+(2v)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{4}+4{v}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{v}^{2}({v}^{2}+1)} \\  & =2v\sqrt{{v}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{v}^{2}}=v$ since $v\ge 0$ on $D.$

Next, let's denote

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le \sqrt{3}}.
$$

Then, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2v\sqrt{{v}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{\int }_{0}^{1}2v\sqrt{{v}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}2v\sqrt{{v}^{2}+1}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}2v\sqrt{{v}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}v\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the substitution 

$$
w={v}^{2}+1\,⇒\,\text{d}w=2v\,\text{d}v,
$$

we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}2v\sqrt{{v}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{w}\,\text{d}w \\  & ={[\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{w}^{3}}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}[\sqrt{{4}^{3}}-\sqrt{{1}^{3}}] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(8-1) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-v⟩$ that is subject to the constraint ${u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 9.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that the region ${u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 9$ corresponds to the disk

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 9},
$$

of radius $3.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{3}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}{∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\sqrt{3}\cdot (\pi \cdot {3}^{2}) \\  & =9\pi \sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface
questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨u+v,\,3{u}^{2},\,u-v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,6u,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3{u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 6u & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}6u & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 6u \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6u,\,2,\,-6u⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-6u,\,2,\,-6u⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-6u)^{2}+(2)^{2}+(-6u)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36{u}^{2}+4+36{u}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{72{u}^{2}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4(18{u}^{2}+1)} \\  & =2\sqrt{18{u}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\sqrt{18{u}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface
questions.problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 2,\,0\le v\le \pi }
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩$ for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le \pi .$ What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-u\operatorname{sin}⁡v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ 0 & 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & -u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & \operatorname{cos}⁡v \\ 0 & -u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ 0 & 2u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u{sin}^{2}⁡v-2u{cos}^{2}⁡v,\,2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩ \\  & =⟨-2u,\,2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-2u,\,2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2u)^{2}+(2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v)^{2}+(4{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}+4{u}^{4}{sin}^{2}⁡v+16{u}^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡v} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}+4{u}^{4}({sin}^{2}⁡v+{cos}^{2}⁡v)+12{u}^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡v} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}+4{u}^{4}+12{u}^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡v} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}(1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v)} \\  & =\sqrt{4{u}^{2}}\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v} \\  & =2u\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $\sqrt{{u}^{2}}=u$ since $u\ge 0$ on $D.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2u\sqrt{1+{u}^{2}+3{u}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡v}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨u-v,\,u+2v,\,2u-v⟩$ that is subject to the constraint ${u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,2,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-5,\,-1,\,3⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-5,\,-1,\,3⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(-5)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+1+9} \\  & =\sqrt{35}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that the region ${u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 1$ corresponds to the disk

$$
D={(u,v)\,:\,{u}^{2}+{v}^{2}\le 1},
$$

of radius $1.$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{35}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{35}{∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & =\sqrt{35}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\sqrt{35}\cdot (\pi \cdot {1}^{2}) \\  & =\pi \sqrt{35}.\end{aligned}
$$
